ai.definition: Fusion energy breakthroughs refer to advancements in achieving controlled, self-sustaining nuclear fusion reactions that can be scaled up for practical applications.
ai.howItWorks: Fusion involves combining light atomic nuclei under extreme temperatures and pressures to form heavier nuclei. This process releases a significant amount of energy without the radioactive waste produced by fission-based reactors. Breakthroughs aim to achieve this in a controlled, stable manner that can be sustained over time for power generation.
ai.problemSolved: These breakthroughs address the challenge of achieving scalable, self-sustaining fusion reactions that could provide a virtually limitless source of clean energy with minimal environmental impact.
ai.manufacturing: Current manufacturing processes involve developing materials and components capable of withstanding extreme temperatures and pressures. This includes developing advanced plasma confinement systems like tokamaks or stellarators, as well as heat-resistant materials for reactor walls.
ai.buildProcess: The build process involves designing and constructing experimental fusion reactors that can maintain the conditions necessary for sustained fusion reactions. This requires precise engineering and integration of various subsystems including magnetic confinement systems, heating mechanisms, and diagnostic equipment.
ai.costDrivers: Key cost drivers include the development of materials that can withstand extreme conditions, the complexity of reactor design, and the high energy input required to initiate and maintain fusion reactions.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook suggests potential for significant advancements in the next decade, with a path towards commercial viability by mid-century if current trends continue.
ai.regulation: Regulatory frameworks are still evolving. There is a need for safety standards and environmental impact assessments as fusion technology moves closer to practical application.
ai.risks: Technical risks include achieving sustained, stable reactions, managing the high energy inputs required, and ensuring reactor safety under extreme conditions. Economic risks involve the high initial investment and long-term financial viability of fusion power plants.
ai.profitability: Profitability is uncertain due to current research status and lack of commercial-scale deployment. However, if successful, it could transform the energy sector by providing a clean, virtually limitless source of power.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will likely focus on improving reactor efficiency, reducing costs, and scaling up experimental reactors for practical applications. Collaboration between academia, industry, and government is crucial to advancing this technology.

glossary.def: The process of combining atomic nuclei under extreme conditions to release energy.
A toroidal-shaped device used for magnetic confinement of plasma in nuclear fusion experiments.
A type of confinement system that uses a non-axisymmetric magnetic field to confine plasma.

subsystems.name: Confinement system
subsystems.role: holds a plasma of light nuclei together long enough and densely enough to fuse — by magnetic fields, by lasers, or by both.

subsystems.name: Plasma heating and control
subsystems.role: raises the fuel to fusion temperature and keeps it stable.

subsystems.name: First wall and neutron blanket
subsystems.role: survives the neutron flux, converts neutron energy to heat and breeds tritium from lithium.

subsystems.name: Exhaust and ash removal
subsystems.role: removes spent helium and the enormous surface heat load.

subsystems.name: Tritium fuel cycle
subsystems.role: extracts bred tritium, cleans it and feeds it back to the plasma.

subsystems.name: Balance of plant
subsystems.role: turns blanket heat into electricity, as in any thermal power station.

buildSteps.title: Choose the confinement route
buildSteps.detail: Magnetic confinement (tokamak, stellarator) or inertial confinement (laser or pulsed power compressing a fuel capsule) — each dictates the whole plant layout.

buildSteps.title: Build the confinement hardware
buildSteps.detail: Superconducting coils wound and cased, or a laser hall with hundreds of beamlines and precise target positioning.

buildSteps.title: Make the vacuum chamber
buildSteps.detail: A torus or reaction chamber fabricated and welded to tight tolerances, then baked and evacuated.

buildSteps.title: Line it for neutrons
buildSteps.detail: Blanket modules with lithium breeder and coolant channels are fitted behind plasma-facing armour.

buildSteps.title: Add heating, fuelling and diagnostics
buildSteps.detail: Injectors, antennas and thousands of sensors are installed and calibrated.

buildSteps.title: Run with hydrogen first
buildSteps.detail: Commission the machine on hydrogen or deuterium, where neutrons are negligible, to tune control.

buildSteps.title: Switch to deuterium–tritium
buildSteps.detail: Introduce tritium, breed it in the blanket, and demonstrate a self-sustaining fuel cycle.

buildSteps.title: Close the electricity loop
buildSteps.detail: Route blanket heat to a turbine and export power — the step no fusion device has yet performed.

prerequisites.tech: Net energy gain from a fusion plasma
prerequisites.why: achieved in a laser experiment in 2022; magnetic devices have not yet matched it.
REBCO tape at roughly 20 tesla has been demonstrated, enabling far smaller magnetic devices.
no tested structural material endures a power-plant neutron dose for years.

prerequisites.tech: Tritium breeding and handling at scale
prerequisites.why: tritium is scarce and radioactive; a plant must breed and recycle its own.
a plant must run for long pulses without instabilities that damage the walls.

pathway.milestone: research machines and laser facilities demonstrating ignition and long-pulse plasmas
pathway.unlocks: confidence that the physics can be engineered.

pathway.milestone: pilot plants aiming for net electricity, using compact high-field magnets or improved stellarators
blanket and tritium test modules inside a burning plasma machine
pathway.unlocks: a closed fuel cycle and validated materials.

pathway.milestone: first demonstration power plants on a grid
pathway.unlocks: firm low-carbon baseload — contingent on materials and fuel breeding, which are unsolved today.
